changes.current_line: Support plans with tiered response times, up to 24/7 coverage.
changes.change: For buyers switching after an outage, especially when the operations owner decides, do not lead with tiers and response times. Lead with people: 'A name, not a queue.' Name the account lead and solutions engineer, give the escalation path (including who covers when that person is away), and offer coverage tied to the buyer's own critical events, for example their on-sale morning. Only make coverage commitments the support/CS lead has confirmed we can staff.
changes.why: The rep walked the decider through the tiers and response times and she called it 'a queue with a faster timer', while the competitor won the room with named people and on-call on-sale coverage.

changes.change: Add a templated one-page critical-event plan for event-driven merchants, to hand to the decider before she asks twice: who is watching during their peak event, who they call, what the escalation path is, and what we do in the first minutes of a failure. Headline it with the buyer's own frame: 'I don't buy uptime, I buy what happens when it's down.'
changes.why: The decider wanted to see 'on paper, what we do on an on-sale morning', the rep admitted 'We don't have that as a thing' and said he could have built it with the solutions engineer.

changes.change: Add a proof point for incident-driven buyers: a short list of event-driven (for example ticketing) customer references who can describe who picked up and what happened during a real peak event or incident, not only vouch for the brand. Use alongside logos, not instead of a named contact.
changes.why: The rep said 'I had logos. I didn't have a person.', and the decider was looking for 'Someone who picks up.'

changes.change: For high-stakes, spiky merchants where an outage triggered the deal, add a decider-level opener for the operations owner: start with what happens in the first minutes of an incident and who answers, then bring in platform proof (load tests, docs, sandbox) as support for the technical team, not as the lead.
changes.why: The switch was triggered when the provider's support replied 'after the on-sale was over', and the sandbox load test that won over the CTO's team drew only 'good' from the decider, who said she buys 'what happens when it's down'.
